column1: # scripts/verify/mutants.tsv - the mutant catalogue
# One row per mutant: the source change that reintroduces the defect a test
# claims to cover. `tests.tsv` selects a mutant by name (`red = mutant:<name>`);
# this file says what that name does. Nothing here is executed: the engine is
# riscv_mutant_apply() in common.cmake, and it treats the file as text -- it
# knows nothing about SystemVerilog.
#   name <TAB> file <TAB> find <TAB> replace <TAB> why
# name      the string tests.tsv names as `mutant:<name>`
# file      path relative to the repository root
# find      the exact text to replace; it must occur EXACTLY once in file,
#           otherwise the mutant is stale and the gate aborts
# replace   the text that reintroduces the defect
# why       one line, printed when the mutant is applied and by --list
# '#' starts a comment line; a comment block above a row is that mutant's
# rationale. `;` is escaped by riscv_tsv_rows()/riscv_tsv_cell(), so SV
# statements with a semicolon are fine in a cell. The root-cause narrative
# stays in doc/verification.md (G-20/G-26/G-27, FR-12); this file only says
# what the mutation does.
# T-06 (FR-12): the pre-fix core ignored the address low bits and always
# extended the byte at the highest address, so 8 of the 12 T-06 cases stored
# the wrong value. Pinning the lane to 3 reproduces exactly that. Since WP-13 P6
# the lane expression starts with the split-load override (`split_wb` puts the
# assembled word at lane 0), so the row pins the ADDRESS half and leaves the
# override alone: the defect is the missing addr[1:0] select, not the split.

column4: assign ld_lane = split_wb ? 2'd0 : 2'b11; // negative control: lane never selected
column5: the sub-word lane is not selected from the address (pre-fix FR-12)

column1: # T-08 (NFR-05): rv32ui-p-simple has no test case; the verdict rests on ADDI
# producing 1 and the store reaching tohost. Ignoring the second operand turns
# `li gp,1` into `li gp,0` and breaks `la t5,tohost`, so the harness must
# report SANITY: TIMEOUT plus a UVM error.
sanity-addi
column4: alu_result = alu_data1.s_data; // negative control: ADD ignores the second operand
column5: ADDI/ADD ignore their second operand, so `li gp,1` writes 0 and the pass store writes 0

column1: # T-09 (WP-4b): T-09 sets is_active=UVM_PASSIVE and requires the monitor only.
# Removing the guard builds the driver/sequencer in passive mode.
passive-agent-always-active
column4: if (1'b1) begin // negative control: UVM_PASSIVE ignored
column5: the agent builds the driver/sequencer even when is_active=UVM_PASSIVE

column1: # T-10 (G-27): reverting pc_id to the current `pc` misaligns the decoder PC by
# one instruction: a branch at 0xa0 targets 0x53c instead of 0x538.
branch-redirect
column4: pc_id <= pc; // negative control: one-instruction PC misalignment
column5: the decoder sees the next instruction's PC, so a branch target is +4 (G-27)

column1: # T-11 (G-26): alu_ex is the EX source of the ALU/jump forwarding; leaving it
# unknown loses the predecessor's value.
forward-rs1
column4: assign alu_ex = 'x; // negative control: EX forward source missing
column5: the EX-stage forward source is unknown, so the predecessor's value is lost (G-26)

column1: # T-12 (G-20): slicing imm[20:0] zero-extends a negative offset and sends the
# branch to the 0x200000-family; rv32ui-p-beq times out.
negative-branch
column4: jump_addr = base_addr + imm[20:0]; // negative control: zero-extended offset
column5: a negative branch/jump offset is zero-extended (G-20)

column1: # T-13 (FR-11 / G-08): rv32ui-p-sb walks every byte lane. The lane shift line is
# shared with the halfword arm since WP-13 P2 (both are byte-granular), so a
# single-line `find` cannot name it any more. The defect is introduced one line
# down instead: the data stays lane-placed, but the strobe always claims lane 0,
# so every SB above lane 0 stores data[7:0] -- which is zero after the rotation
# -- into byte 0 and writes nothing to the addressed byte.
store-lane-offset
column4: data_wr_strb_ex = 4'b0001; // negative control: byte strobe ignores the lane
column5: the byte strobe always claims lane 0, so a byte store above lane 0 writes nothing (G-08)

column1: # T-14 (FR-11 / G-22): rv32ui-p-sh stores at offsets 0 and 2. A halfword
# strobe of 4'b1111 contradicts the halfword width and claims two bytes the
# store did not drive.
store-strb-all
column4: data_wr_strb_ex = 4'b1111; // negative control: halfword strobe drives all four bytes
column5: a halfword store announces four bytes (G-22)

column1: # T-15 (FR-11 / G-08, G-22): rv32ui-p-st_ld mixes byte, half and word. Forcing
# the width port to byte makes every halfword/word store report 2'b00 next to a
# 2- or 4-bit strobe, which the strb_checker rejects even when the image's own
# software verdict would pass.
store-width-cast
column4: assign data_rd_wr_ctrl = 2'b00; // negative control: width port forced to byte
column5: the width port reports byte for every access (FR-11, the old one-bit cast)

column1: # T-16 (FR-17 / G-30): rv32ui-p-ld_st branches at 0xa4 on `sp`, which the load
# at 0x9c has just written and is still in MA. The frozen branch re-evaluates
# correctly one cycle later, but the stale echo of the first decision is
# registered without the qualifier, so the fetch that follows the branch is
# flushed and the image loses the instruction at 0xa8. Reverting the redirect
# alone (`if (branch_taken)`) does NOT reproduce: with the echo still qualified
# the held branch recovers, so the mutant targets the registered echo.
branch-taken-stale
column4: branch_taken_q <= branch_taken; // negative control: stale branch echo
column5: a stale branch decision is echoed and flushes the fetch that follows the branch (G-30)

column1: # T-17 (FR-07 / G-31): rv32ui-p-jalr computes its target from a register the
# previous instruction produced. Closing the jump-forward mux to cond_jump
# leaves that rs1 stale, so every JALR after its producer jumps to the wrong
# place and the image never reaches tohost (the original G-31 timeout).
jalr-no-forward
column4: cond_jump)) begin // negative control: JALR rs1 not forwarded
column5: a JALR target reads a stale rs1 because the jump-forward mux is closed (G-31)

column1: # T-37 (FR-07): the local image jumps through an odd address. With the mask
# removed the target stays odd; the word-indexed image memory still returns the
# word at the aligned address, but the unaligned PC makes the test's PC-relative
# `la` compute linkaddr_3 + 1 and its `bne` sends the image to fail (testnum 3).
jalr-keep-bit0
column4: jump_addr = jump_addr; // negative control: JALR target keeps bit 0
column5: an odd JALR target is not masked to an instruction boundary (FR-07)

column1: # T-29..T-36 (FR-01): SUB, SLL, SLT, SLTU, XOR, SRL, SRA and OR read their
# second operand from rs2 (directly or through the EX/MA/WB forward muxes).
# Selecting the immediate side for every op makes each of them compute with 0
# instead of rs2; the I-type instructions used to build the test data (`li`,
# `la`) are unaffected, so the image reports the failing TESTNUM.
alu-ignore-rs2
column4: case (IMM_S2) // negative control: every ALU op reads the immediate side
column5: the ALU second operand ignores rs2, so the R-type instructions compute with the immediate

column1: # T-23..T-28 (FR-02/FR-03): SLTI, SLTIU, XORI, SRLI, SRAI and ANDI take their
# second operand from the immediate port. Zeroing that port makes the result
# independent of the encoded immediate, but it also breaks the PC-relative `la`
# that builds the tohost address, so these images reach the pass/fail ceremony
# with a wrong store address and the harness times out (SANITY: TIMEOUT,
# UVM_RESULT: FAIL) instead of storing a TESTNUM. The image fails either way.
imm-zero
column4: alu_data2 = '0; // negative control: immediate operand is zero
column5: the ALU immediate operand is zero, so the I-type instructions compute with 0

column1: # T-19..T-22 (FR-08): BLT, BGE, BLTU and BGEU are checked with both taken and
# not-taken cases. Forcing branch_taken for every conditional branch sends the
# not-taken cases (and every `bne ..., fail` guard) down the taken path, so the
# image stores a nonzero TESTNUM to tohost.
branch-always-taken
column4: if (cond_jump) branch_taken = 1'b1; else if (cond_jump) begin // negative control: every conditional branch taken
column5: every conditional branch is taken, so the not-taken cases reach `fail` (FR-08)

column1: # T-18 (FR-06): rv32ui-p-jal checks the link register and the branch target of
# JAL. Dropping the offset makes the jump target the instruction's own PC, so
# the core loops on the JAL forever and the harness never sees tohost.
jal-offset-zero
column4: jump_addr = base_addr; // negative control: jump target drops the offset
column5: JAL jumps to its own PC instead of PC+offset (FR-06)

column1: # T-38 reuses `branch-always-taken` above (FR-08): rv32ui-p-bne has both taken
# and not-taken cases, and every `bne ..., fail` guard is taken, so the image
# reports a nonzero TESTNUM.
# T-39 (FR-02): rv32ui-p-ori takes its function from the ALU_OR arm. The body
# line `alu_result = alu_data1 | alu_data2;` cannot be the `find` of a TSV row
# (a cell may not contain `|`, it is the table separator), so the same defect
# is introduced one line up: the case selector routes ALU_OR into the AND arm,
# and ORI computes AND. Test 2 expects 0xffffff0f and reads 0xff00ff00, so the
# image reaches `fail`; the ceremony's own `ori gp,gp,1` then stores 0x0, which
# the checker reports as SANITY: FAIL testnum=0.
alu-or-to-and
column4: case (alu_op == ALU_OR ? ALU_AND : alu_op) // negative control: OR computes AND
column5: ALU_OR is routed into the AND arm, so ORI writes the bitwise AND (FR-02)

column1: # T-40 (FR-03): rv32ui-p-slli checks SLLI at shifts 0, 1, 7, 14 and 31. Keeping
# data1 and dropping the shift matches only shift 0, so TESTNUM 3 reports.
shift-left-zero
column4: alu_result = alu_data1; // negative control: the left shift is dropped
column5: SLL/SLLI return the unshifted first operand (FR-03)

column1: # T-41 (FR-04): rv32ui-p-lui reads the upper immediate back (`lui ra,0xfffff;
# srai ra,1` == -2048). Sending the LUI arm to ALU_ADD does NOT reproduce it:
# the rs1 field of those U-type encodings selects x0/x31/a6, all still zero, so
# rd is still the immediate. Zeroing the shared U-type immediate does, and the
# image reports TESTNUM 3. The same row also reaches AUIPC, which has its own
# mutant below.
lui-ignores-imm
column4: imm.s_data = '0; // negative control: U-type immediate zero
column5: LUI ignores its upper immediate and writes 0 (FR-04)

column1: # T-42 (FR-05): the decoder sets `alu_src1 = PC;` for AUIPC, but that line
# occurs three times (AUIPC, JAL, JALR) and a `find` must be unique. The defect
# is the same one arm up: PC_S1 in ALU mux 1 returns rs1, so AUIPC adds rs1
# (== x0 in this image) instead of pc and the image reports TESTNUM 5. The
# JAL/JALR link values move too; each of those has its own mutant.
auipc-no-pc
column4: alu_data1 = rs1; // negative control: the pc is not added
column5: AUIPC adds rs1 instead of pc, so rd is the immediate alone (FR-05)

column1: # T-44 (G-28 / C-16): the retire observation is only meaningful if a slot that
# never held a real instruction does not retire. The flush path zeroes inst_ex
# and valid_ex together, so the bubble that follows every flush is invisible to
# WB. Forcing valid_ex for every enabled slot sends that bubble (pc=0, word=0)
# to write-back, where the probe publishes it and the retire checker reports it
# as not the program's next instruction.
retire-every-slot
column4: valid_ex <= 1'b1; // negative control: every pipeline slot retires
column5: a flushed slot retires as if it were an instruction (G-28)

column1: # T-50 (FR-41 / G-33): the reset branch of the PC register. Reverting it to the
# pre-WP-11 `pc <= 'b0` makes the first fetch after reset present 0x0 while the
# harness places the program at RESET_VECTOR (0x8000_0000), so the BFM answers
# nothing, the monitor publishes no fetch and the reset checker's claim is never
# measured -- the test's clock timeout raises the UVM_ERROR. This is the defect
# G-33 records, not a synthetic one.
reset-vector-zero
column4: pc <= 'b0; // negative control: the reset vector is not applied
column5: the first fetch after reset presents 0x0 instead of RESET_VECTOR (G-33)

column1: # T-51 (FR-11 / FR-12 / G-34): a halfword is byte-granular since WP-13 P2, so
# offset 1 occupies bytes 1-2. Both halves of the defect are named here because
# `riscv_mutant_apply()` applies every row of a given name: the load lane and the
# store strobe each round addr[0] away. Reverting both reproduces the pre-fix
# halfword-granular lane (16 * addr[1]) on the read and the write path at once --
# LH at offset 1 returns bytes 0-1 and SH at offset 1 strobes 0011 instead of
halfword-lane-ignore-bit0
column4: assign ld_lane_half = {ld_lane[1], 1'b0}; // negative control: the load halfword lane ignores bit 0
column5: the halfword lane is halfword-granular, so offset 1 reads and strobes bytes 0-1 instead of 1-2 (G-34)

column1: halfword-lane-ignore-bit0
column4: data_wr_strb_ex = 4'b0011 << {alu_result.u_data[1], 1'b0}; // negative control: the store halfword strobe ignores bit 0
column5: the halfword lane is halfword-granular, so offset 1 reads and strobes bytes 0-1 instead of 1-2 (G-34)

column1: # T-53 (FR-38 / G-18): the pre-fix stall was `if (!data_ready && mux_sel_rd_wb)`,
# so a store drove its strobe for one cycle whatever the grant did. The fix's
# line contains `||`, and a TSV cell may not (it is the table separator: splice
# the fix's condition into a row and the reader splits the `find` at the pipes,
# measured -- the `find` came back as `(!data_ready && (mux_sel_rd_wb ` and every
# later column shifted, so the row would abort as incomplete). As in T-39/T-42 the
# defect is therefore introduced one token over: tying the store term of the
# condition to 1'b0 leaves exactly `!data_ready && mux_sel_rd_wb` -- the pre-fix
# expression -- and the `data_wr_en_ma` port the fix added goes unused, as it was.
store-grant-ignored
column4: 1'b0)) begin // negative control: the store does not wait for the grant
column5: a store that does not wait for the grant drives its strobe for one cycle whatever data_ready does, so a withholding memory loses it (G-18)

column1: # T-52 (FR-42 / G-22): P6 landed the two-beat split (rtl/misaligned_split.sv):
# an access whose lane plus width crosses the word is presented as two
# word-aligned beats, so `rv32ui-p-ma_data` reaches its own pass ceremony. Tying
# the detection to 0 reverts it to the pre-P6 world: one beat at the unaligned
# address, which the image rejects at MISALIGNED_LOAD_TEST(3, lw, s0, 1). The
# `find` is line 108 verbatim; it contains no `|`, so the row parses to five
# cells (the `store-grant-ignored` limitation above does not apply here).
no-misaligned-split
column4: assign split_needed = 1'b0; // negative control: the split is disabled
column5: a crossing access is presented as one beat at the unaligned address (FR-42/G-22)

column1: # T-03 (FR-50 / FR-24, WP-14): `csr-illegal-noop` removes the illegal-CSR
# trap. It has two arms in rtl/instruction_decode.sv -- an address the
# configuration does not implement (the `legal = 1'b0; // FR-50: absent
# address` arm) and a write to a read-only address (the
# `if (csr_write && csr_read_only(...)) legal = 1'b0;` arm). Each row flips
# one arm from illegal to legal; riscv_mutant_apply() applies EVERY row of a
# given name, so the tree the test runs on has neither and an illegal CSR
# access retires as a no-operation that writes nothing -- the defect FR-50
# names. One arm alone already costs T-03 a trap, but the mutant of a named
# defect is the whole defect.
csr-illegal-noop
column4: legal = 1'b1; // negative control: an absent CSR address decodes as legal
column5: an absent CSR address retires as a no-operation instead of raising cause 2 (FR-50)

column1: csr-illegal-noop
column4: if (csr_write && csr_read_only(inst.csr_type.csr)) legal = 1'b1; // negative control: a write to a read-only CSR decodes as legal
column5: a write to a read-only CSR address retires as a no-operation instead of raising cause 2 (FR-50)

column1: # T-03 (FR-50 / FR-24 / FR-37 / FR-32 / FR-49, WP-14b batch 2a): the six
# independent clauses T-03's program measures besides the illegal-CSR trap, plus
# the D12b pulse contract. Each names a different defect, so each is its own
# (T-03, mutant) pair in the red cell.
# D5: the Zicsr write rule is the REGISTER SPECIFIER. `csrrs x15, mhartid, x0`
# must not write, so it must NOT trap; a core that always writes turns that read
# of a read-only CSR into cause 2 and T-03 loses a retire.
csr-write-always
column4: ? 1'b1 : 1'b1; // negative control: every CSRRS/CSRRC writes
column5: CSRRS/CSRRC with rs1=x0 writes instead of suppressing, so a read of a read-only CSR traps (D5, FR-50)

column1: # FR-29: the program computes mtvec with AUIPC+ADDI and places the handler at
# +0x200. A fixed vector sends the trap to 1000, where the program has nothing.
trap-vector-fixed
column4: assign mtvec_base = 32'd1000; // negative control: the trap vector is fixed
column5: trap entry redirects to 1000 instead of the mtvec.BASE the program wrote (FR-29)

column1: # FR-23: mepc is the PC of the instruction that trapped. Capturing pc+4 makes
# the handler return one instruction past the trap site, and the co-cycle CSR
# read (and the handler's own read) then disagrees by value.
mepc-off-by-one
column4: mepc_q   <= trap_pc + 32'd4; // negative control: mepc captures pc+4
column5: mepc captures pc+4 instead of the trapping instruction's PC (FR-23)

column1: # FR-37: misa is the CONFIGURED extension set. A literal that advertises A
# (bit 0) on an RV32I-only build contradicts `misa_value(ENABLE_A/M/C)`.
misa-literal
column4: CSR_MISA:      csr_rdata = 32'h4000_0101; // negative control: misa is a literal
column5: misa reads a literal that advertises A instead of misa_value(ENABLE_A/M/C) (FR-37)

column1: # FR-32 / D13: T-03 drives hart_id = 5. A hardwired zero passes only if the
# test also drove zero, which it does not.
mhartid-zero
column4: CSR_MHARTID:   csr_rdata = 32'h0000_0000;             // negative control: mhartid reads zero
column5: mhartid reads 0 instead of hart_id, which the test drives as 5 (FR-32)

column1: # FR-49 / D13: time and timeh are views of the observed mtime. T-03 drives
# 0x0000_0001_2345_6789, so a hardwired zero is a value mismatch, not a guess.
# The two halves are separate rows (as halfword-lane-ignore-bit0 is): the same
# defect on the read path, one per line with a unique find.
time-not-a-view
column4: CSR_TIME:      csr_rdata = 32'h0000_0000;            // negative control: time is not a view
column5: time does not follow mtime, so the observed 64-bit timer is not what time reads (FR-49)

column1: time-not-a-view
column4: CSR_TIMEH:     csr_rdata = 32'h0000_0000;            // negative control: timeh is not a view
column5: timeh does not follow mtime, so the observed 64-bit timer is not what timeh reads (FR-49)

column1: # D12b: trap_valid is the edge the pipeline advances, not a level. Replacing the
# IF/ID and ID/EX enable terms with the global enable leaves it high while a
# split beat or a data grant holds those registers (T-03 has neither, but the
# defect is the signal's contract, not a stimulus path -- see the report).
trap-held-while-stalled
column4: clk_en; // negative control: the stage enables do not gate trap_valid
column5: trap_valid ignores the pipeline enables, so it stays high while a split beat or a data grant holds the pipeline (D12b)

column1: # T-62's defect (FR-22/D12): the IF/ID and ID/EX enables are exactly what
# split_stall and the data wait take away, so tying them to 1 makes the trap a
# level across the held crossing store and the monitor publishes it once per
# cycle -- `expected_traps_exact` names the count.
trap-valid-while-held
column4: 1'b1; // negative control: trap_valid ignores the IF/ID and ID/EX enables
column5: trap_valid ignores the IF/ID and ID/EX enables, so it stays high across a held beat (T-62's defect)

column1: # T-60's defect (WP-14b audit blocker 1, FR-22/FR-23/FR-25): the retire in WB is
# OLDER than the trap in ID, so the commit must be published first. Publishing
# the sampled trap before the retire block (and clearing it so the final
# publication is a no-op) makes the model apply the trap first; its prediction
# for the co-cycle CSR read is then the POST-trap mepc/mcause.
trap-published-first
column4: publish_trap(trp); trp = null; if (retire_vif.retire_valid) begin
column5: the monitor publishes the trap before the commit of the same cycle, so the model applies the trap first (T-60's defect)

column1: # T-61's defect (FR-22/G-37): `exception` is a DUT input carried by the
# interface. Tying the DUT port to zero leaves the driver's request and the
# monitor's observation on a wire the core never sees, so the external arm of
# proc_trap_priority is unreachable again.
exception-unrouted
column4: .exception(4'b0000), // negative control: the external cause is not routed
column5: the DUT's exception input is tied to zero, so the platform's request never reaches the trap path (T-61's defect)
